title: AHU-1 Freezestat Bypass and Frozen Cooling-Coil Burst
description: A deliberately failed freezestat allows subfreezing mixed air to remain on a stagnant chilled-water coil. Ice develops over 20 simulated minutes and the cooling coil ultimately ruptures and floods the mechanical area.

events.description: Bypass the automatic freezestat to represent a failed or improperly commissioned low-temperature cutout
Fail the physical outside-air damper fully open so the mixed-air low-limit command cannot protect the coil
Run the supply fan so cold outside air crosses the coils
Drive the outside-air damper fully open
Leave chilled water stagnant so the no-flow 20-minute exposure path is demonstrated

expected_results: The failed-open outside-air damper defeats the mixed-air low-limit command and cooling-coil entering air remains below 32 degrees F while the bypassed freezestat does not shut the fan
The freeze-condition point activates and the ice indication increases with simulated exposure
At 20 simulated minutes of continuous subfreezing exposure without proven chilled-water flow, the cooling-coil burst/flood alarm latches
The AHU command-center graphic changes to the frozen cooling-coil and flooded-floor state
completion_criteria: Student identifies cold outside air, loss of preheat, the failed-open outside-air damper, and the bypassed freezestat as the initiating chain
Student explains why a functioning low-temperature cutout must stop the fan, close outside air, and place the water coil in its configured protective valve state
instructor_notes: Run at 60x simulation speed to complete the 20-simulated-minute exposure in about 20 seconds of wall time. This deliberately combines a failed-open OA damper with a bypassed freezestat; the working mixed-air low-limit still commands closed but cannot move the failed actuator. The 20/60-minute damage model is a training approximation; real coil-freeze risk depends on fluid temperature, flow, glycol, geometry, and weather. Use Restart after the exercise to repair the latched coil burst and clear forces/faults.
student_objectives: Diagnose a compound freeze-protection failure from air temperature, valve, fan, and safety evidence
Understand why a freezestat is installed as a serpentine low-limit element across the coil face rather than as a single averaging air-temperature point
